# markdown-s1 — Minimal Markdown → HTML renderer (tier S1) ## Module: `src/markdown.js` (ES module) `export function render(markdown: string): string` → HTML. Output must follow CommonMark 0.31 HTML output (as produced by the reference implementation commonmark.js) for the following subset. Insignificant whitespace between block-level tags does not matter; `
`/`
` and ``/`` are equivalent. - ATX headings `#` … `######`. - Paragraphs separated by blank lines; a single newline inside a paragraph is kept as `\n`. - Emphasis `*a*` / `_a_` → ``, strong `**a**` / `__a__` → `` (no intraword `_` emphasis). - Inline code `` `x` ``. - Links `[text](url)` and `[text](url "title")`, images `![alt](src)`. - Unordered lists (`-` or `*`) and ordered lists (`1.`, with `start` attribute when not starting at 1), single level, tight. - Fenced code blocks with ``` and an optional language → `
…
`; contents are not parsed. - Blockquotes (`> `, single level). - Thematic break `---` on its own line (not under a paragraph line). - Escape `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` in text, code and attributes. Raw HTML is never passed through (it is escaped as text). .: PROVENANCE.json SPEC.md package.json tests ./tests: public ./tests/public: smoke.test.js

python3 - <<'EOF'
p='src/markdown.js'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("if (!blankPending && !startsBlock(x) && lastIsParagraph(body))","if (!blankPending && !listMarker(x) && !startsBlock(x) && lastIsParagraph(body))")
s=s.replace("if (trailing && i < lines.length && listMarker(lines[i]) && !isHr(lines[i])) sawBlankBetween = true;","{ const nm = i < lines.length && listMarker(lines[i]); if (trailing && nm && !isHr(lines[i]) && nm.bullet === first.bullet && nm.ch === first.ch) sawBlankBetween = true; }")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
cat > t.mjs <<'EOF'
import {render} from './src/markdown.js';
for (const s of ['- a\n- b\n\n1. x\n1. y\n\n3. q\n4. r','[a](</u r>) [b](http://x.com/a "t") a * b','- a\n  - b\n- c'])
 console.log(render(s),'\n=====');
EOF
node t.mjs; rm t.mjs
echo '[]' > PROVENANCE.json
cat > PROVENANCE.json <<'EOF'
[]
EOF
node --test 2>&1 | grep -E "^# (pass|fail)"
